scope: Three studies per approach, six approaches plus three surprises. Original Breachline designs informed by the named broad visual directions. New mechanics, cultures, taxa, technology levels and faction ownership remain proposals.

groups.title: A - Closest to current Breachline
groups.direction: Restrained, intimate and useful magic; observed human feeling, simple well-made objects and subject-specific effects.
groups.style: STYLE: The closest fit to the recently liked Breachline studies. Economical naturalistic painting, quiet distinctive magic, clear construction, warm/cool light chosen for the scene. Avoid a loud aura or energy-thread vocabulary.

groups.title: B - High fantasy
groups.direction: More openly wondrous, elegant and ceremonial: light, noble silhouettes and magical creatures.
groups.style: STYLE: Push toward luminous classical HIGH FANTASY: elegant elongated silhouettes, fine worked metal, rich jewel colors, graceful ceremonial shapes and clearly visible wonder. Magic may be more overt and beautiful than the baseline, while materials and anatomy remain credible. Distinct original designs.

groups.title: C - Steampunk
groups.direction: A stronger industrial edge: useful boilers, load-bearing mechanisms and larger working machines.
groups.style: STYLE: Push toward convincing STEAMPUNK with high-fantasy craft. Dark iron, warm brass, copper, ceramic insulation, rivets where plates join, actual valves, pistons and working mechanisms. Every major component has a readable purpose; fewer large functional forms instead of ornamental gear confetti. Steam stays physical. No flying machine, automatic modern weapon or default goggles.

groups.title: D - Arcane-inspired
groups.direction: Sharper tailoring, angular design, social texture and saturated magical technology.
groups.style: STYLE: Explore an ARCANE-INSPIRED direction through angular tailored silhouettes, expressive individually shaped faces, faceted painted planes, rich teal/cobalt/amber contrasts and urban magical craft. It remains an oil/acrylic concept painting with visible brushwork. Translate the design language into original Breachline people and objects; no recognizable Arcane characters, outfits, symbols or copied devices. A stronger color and stylization experiment.

groups.title: E - Warcraft-inspired
groups.direction: Broad heroic silhouettes, oversized crafted gear, bold color and powerful creature forms.
groups.style: STYLE: Explore a WARCRAFT-INSPIRED heroic fantasy edge: broad weighty graphic silhouettes, larger hands and shoulders, monumental armor shapes, thick readable weapons, bold saturated accents and forceful poses. Carry it with painterly material richness, not cartoon outlines or toy-like CGI. Exaggeration is deliberate but construction and weight remain legible. Invent Breachline designs, no copied faction emblems or recognizable game characters.

groups.title: F - LOTR-inspired
groups.direction: Old-world craft, weathered nobility and quiet mythic scale, with magic often suggested.
groups.style: STYLE: Explore a LORD OF THE RINGS-INSPIRED direction: patient mythic atmosphere, natural proportions, deep history through materials, exquisite modest craft, weathered cloth and quiet nobility. Grounded medieval fantasy with subtle wonder and a strong sense of place. No copied film costumes, actor likenesses, White Tree, One Ring inscription or established Middle-earth characters. Entirely original Breachline subjects.

groups.title: G - Three wild cards
groups.direction: Desert mineral divination, maritime lacquer armor and an uncanny shadow companion.
groups.style: STYLE: A deliberate surprise at the edge of Breachline: choose the particular visual language described below. Keep compelling painted materials, clear silhouette and human-scale storytelling. Fresh cultural and magical possibilities, not fixed setting facts.

images.title: Graveside listener
images.intent: A quiet conversation with an uncertain shade builds on the loved necromancy and communal rites.
images.boundary: Tests an intimate spirit encounter; neither the nature of souls nor an afterlife is established.
images.brief: A mature human woman about 52 with a long crooked nose, soft heavy eyelids, tied dark-gray hair and a thoughtful, rather kind face, in a plain dark plum wool coat and slate skirt, kneels beside an empty low stone seat in a sparse burial courtyard. She holds no casting device and is gently speaking, palms resting naturally on her knees. On the seat is a faint incomplete elderly human silhouette, made of soft gray translucent shadow, concentrated around bowed shoulders and a suggested profile; the ground remains visible through it. No skeleton costume, gore, skull jewelry, chains, light strings or spectral beam. A humble sprig laid at the seat and worn stone establish attention and care. The scene feels like patient listening, not a theatrical summoning. Late warm daylight touches the listener while the shade remains cool. Right details: her individual face; her ordinary hands and the boundary where the faint shade meets the seat.

images.title: Storm at the ford

images.title: Glasshouse annealer
images.intent: A craft specialist controls heat in fresh glass, extending the useful-magic direction.
images.boundary: Tests specialist manufacture, not instant repair, mass production or a required power system.
images.brief: An adult female goblin glass artisan with olive-brown skin, large expressive ears, a broad long nose, narrow eyes and strong adult wiry proportions, graying dark hair in a practical knot. No childlike or glamorous human face. She wears rolled cream linen sleeves and a simple soot-gray apron. At a modest workbench beside an ordinary small furnace she passes a bare hand close to a freshly formed deep green glass vessel held securely by an iron tool in her other hand. The magic changes how heat settles WITHIN the unbroken glass: a warm amber zone moves into cool emerald clarity, with a tiny shimmering optical distortion near the surface. No glowing threads, holograms or magic bracelets. This is finishing new glass, NOT repairing broken pottery or reversing time. A second finished thick glass cup, ordinary glassblowing pipe and wooden shaping tool provide clear craft context. Right details: adult face and hand; the translucent vessel with warm-to-cool depth. Beautiful transmitted light, modest useful work.

images.title: Dawnward cavalier
images.intent: An elegant sacred warrior pushes toward brighter ceremonial high fantasy.
images.boundary: Tests a more luminous Vigil reading; no divine intervention or standard uniform is established.
images.brief: A tall dignified male lion-folk oath champion with an unmistakably feline lion head, believable muzzle and ears, dark tawny mane and focused amber eyes. images.title: Starwell scholar
images.intent: Scholarly magic becomes openly wondrous, with an elegant caster and a small impossible night sky.
images.boundary: Tests spectacle and refined courtly styling without requiring an optical device.
images.brief: An exceptionally beautiful yet distinctive human woman scholar around 38, warm brown skin, strong aquiline nose, widely set dark eyes, thick black hair swept into a low twist, one slightly raised eyebrow. A long midnight-blue silk-and-wool gown with a simple silver embroidered collar and structured cream over-robe, dignified and practical enough to move in, not a superhero bodysuit. She stands on a low observatory terrace with her hands apart around a hovering shallow disc of impossible midnight space, about a meter across: a tiny deep starfield with a bright crescent-like reflection, softly lighting her face in blue. It is direct scholarly spellcraft, no telescope, goggles, machine, floating formula or thread network. A few angular stone fragments float immediately above the disc as part of the controlled magical demonstration; no flight vehicle. Two details: her expressive appealing face in reflected starlight; the disc's dark depth beside a plain sleeve and hand. Purple dusk, sapphire and ivory, graceful high fantasy with selective radiant light.

images.title: Lockyard tug

images.title: Foundry strider
images.intent: A large working automaton makes its mechanical purpose and locomotion visible.
images.boundary: Tests a stronger industrial construct edge; autonomy and prevalence remain open.
images.brief: A three-meter-tall steam-driven foundry automaton shaped for handling heavy hot stock, not a human in armor. images.title: The second shadow
images.intent: An ordinary goblin has an impossible second shadow that behaves like a protector.
images.boundary: A folklore-like surprise: the companion's identity and source are left unresolved.
images.brief: DESIGN DIRECTION: uncanny intimate folk fantasy with visual wit, nearly no luminous effects. An ordinary adult goblin ferryman with olive-brown skin, a long blunt nose, broad pointed ears, mature wiry proportions and a gently amused lined face, in a simple ochre wool jacket and patched slate trousers. He stands at ease beside a mooring post on a modest evening quay, holding a short ordinary boat pole with both hands. A single warm lantern low at image-left casts his SMALL NORMAL goblin shadow onto the plaster wall behind him. Beside that shadow is a SECOND, MUCH LARGER impossible shadow shaped like a watchful long-eared wolf-like beast. The beast exists ONLY as a dark flat silhouette on the wall, no physical animal and no glowing outline. Its raised paw and turned head differ unmistakably from the goblin's still posture; it seems to watch the lane for him. Make the two shadows visually distinct and the impossible relationship easy to understand. No threat to viewer, cables, puppetry strings or comic expression. Warm lantern, dusk-blue quay and textured pale wall. Right details: the goblin's ordinary face; the edge of the beast shadow across wall and ground. Quiet humor and strange companionship, an original magical possibility.
